questions.question: What should happen to RFC-0019 now that only its CI lane is still open?

options.label: Leave as Draft (Recommended)
options.description: No change now. ID-266 rewrites it when the CI lane starts, after BK-408 changes the pass conditions. The Status block already says what was replaced.

options.label: Start BK-408 now
options.description: Change the Roadmap pass conditions to judge on net time saved, as the first step toward rewriting the CI lane. Small item, done on its own branch.

options.label: Withdraw and replace
options.description: Mark RFC-0019 Withdrawn, keeping its Phase 0 history, and write a new RFC for only the CI lane, possibly reusing fast_gate.py. ID-266 and BK-408 then point to the new RFC.

questions.question: Scope for BK-408? Orientation found one item that affects it: ID-266 owns the CI lane and the RFC rewrite. BUG-302, BUG-306 and ID-268 don't affect it.

options.label: Change exits 2–3 only (Recommended)
options.description: Rewrite the Phase 2 and 3 pass conditions and D7.4's zero-escape sentence around net time saved, with each escape costed as one full run (the bucket-rules / fast-gate standard). Keep Phase 0's row as it ran, with a note. Close BK-408. Selector, lane design and full rewrite stay with ID-266.

options.label: Also mark local phases replaced
options.description: Do the above, and also mark the Phase 1 and Phase 2 local deliverables (pilot selector, local fast target) as replaced by hatch run fast, so the Roadmap only describes the CI path. Bigger change that starts on ID-266's rewrite.

options.label: Change all three, Phase 0 too
options.description: Apply the new standard to Phase 0's row as well. This rewrites the bar Phase 0 was actually measured against, so the record of its stop decision changes after the fact.
